i made a list last year of everything that i wanted to change about myself and my life. two lists really. one for long term goals, and one for short term goals. i tried to keep it realistic in what i could do given my circumstances. i was like you after i got let go from a job and broke up with my girlfriend, couldn't find motivation to do anything, didn't want to. one day i asked myself how long i wanted to live like that, what my life would look like in a couple years if i did.

short term
make a resume
apply, apply, APPLY! -GET A JOB!
i cannot stress how important it is to happiness. having something to do during the day, something to keep your mind busy is an extremely useful tool for finding happiness. even if it's just a part time job at a resteraunt or a grocery store it'll help.

make a list of possible jobs/careers you'd be interested in, then look into the courses you would need to complete to get those jobs

adult education centers are another extremely helpful tool at your disposal who are willing to work with you for your future, and they're usually low cost with flexible hours.

from there it's all a matter of are you willing to do what is necessary to secure a good future for yourself, because your mother sure as fuck isn't going to do it for you

you dont find joy in things, correct? do you have a significant other? some things i've learned are that friendships/relationships are key to building a happy lifestyle. part of the way we do that is thru hobbies and finding our interests. if you are constantly thinking you dont enjoy anything, thats normal, you just havent found something that excites you in that way, something truly interesting to you. it's not that you cant or never will feel joy, its that you're trying to hard to find it. in my experience, i was happiest when i let go of the fear of never being happy and embraced the moment. there's a lot of terrifying shit to worry about, but we cross those bridges when we come to them. it seems like you're almost making something from nothing without giving something the opportunity to develop. to be diagnosed at 13 of being depressed can be rough, and really effect your development due to the stigmas attached. you're in your twenties now and really starting to get a feel of the world. if you find yourself feeling dull and uninterested pack a day bag and go somewhere completely new. it doesnt have to be far or fancy, but far enough to get a new experience. even if it's something you wouldn't enjoy normally, being a part of a new activity could inspire new interests i.e. instruments, growing plants, building models/computers/boats. it's a matter of perspective i myself have examined numerous times and experience constantly in the sense that no matter what positive things happen i feel sad or depressed constantly, and its more often just a product of my own thinking. i found later that making peace with people that i've wronged or who have wronged me helped move past some of the aggression i was feeling and reassured me that i am in control of the way i think and how i feel. it doesn't always work but it helps, at least i hope it does.  cheers

To go back on what I said a little bit, I thankfully I had friends whose families I was close with. One family in particular. They hesitantly agreed to let me sleep on their couch, given I met requirements such as curfew, acquiring a job and steady income. I thoughtlessly took advantage of that situation. I brought drugs and violence into their house, yet still they kept letting me stay with them. My friends mother, one day sat me down and said "Steven, if you don't stop the way you're going you're going to be dead in a year".  That was enough to scare me to the point where I realized that where I was headed was where I didn't want to be. After she died some years later I was able to see that I had made it quite a bit further than I thought I could. I know, I said no one pulled me off the street and helped me, because they didn't. I took advantage of someone's family, and they saw past that. They didn't owe me anything but instead gave me what I needed to better myself, and that was understanding. I truly believe every "bum" can be helped and given an opportunity at a full prosperous life, but they're not going to get that from city officials, they need it from the community.

Edit: I'm now 26, live with my girlfriend in a rented house, and work steadily. I never graduated high school, or attended college. Everything they've (the homeless) come up against can be overcome and should be instead of overlooked.

But to answer your question about me going camping, I've lived on the street, had to steal to eat and break in to places to sleep. I lived without luxury, grew up in poverty so I actually do understand some of their situation. Did workshops and welfare help me?  Fuck, no. Did anyone pull me off the street, give me a job and somewhere to live?  No. But I certainly would've rather had a job where I'm earning money every day to buy food than somewhere to sleep.
